title: Degree of the line-bundle homomorphism is the Euler-characteristic square
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $A/k$ be an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety] of dimension $g\geq1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_A$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Write $\chi(A,M)=\sum_{i\geq0}(-1)^i\dim_kH^i(A,M)\in\mathbf Z$ for coherent Zariski Euler characteristic [def-pc-euler-characteristic]; for an invertible $M$ this is a finite sum of finite dimensions. Let $\phi_L:A\to A^\vee$ be the homomorphism $x\mapsto[t_x^*L\otimes L^{-1}]$ of [lem-sfb-abelian-polarization-calculus]. For a group-scheme homomorphism $h:A\to A^\vee$ [def-sc-group-scheme], set $d(h)=\dim_k\Gamma(\ker h,\mathcal O_{\ker h})$ if $h$ is an isogeny [def-sc-isogeny], and set $d(h)=0$ otherwise. Then $$d(\phi_L)=\chi(A,L)^2\quad\text{in }\mathbf Z.$$ No ampleness or finite-kernel hypothesis is imposed on $L$.

source.place: Chapter I, Theorem 11.1(a), printed p.54 (PDF p.60), with the degree-zero convention preceding Theorem 10.9, printed p.46 (PDF p.52).

proof.text: By [lem-sc-abelian-variety-projective] choose a projective embedding of $A$ and let $H$ be the pullback of $\mathcal O(1)$. Thus $H$ is very ample and in particular ample. Its coordinate sections have affine nonvanishing opens covering $A$: these are the closed subschemes cut out by $A$ in the standard affine charts of projective space. Hence $H$ is also ample in the absolute affine-locus sense used below. Put $M_n=L\otimes H^{\otimes n}$ for $n\geq0$. The variety $A$ is proper and Noetherian, and these invertible modules are coherent (locally they are free of rank one over the Noetherian structure sheaf). The finiteness assertion in [lem-pc-euler-characteristic-well-defined] makes all their Euler characteristics well defined.

source.place: I, Theorem 6.4 (projectivity); elementary choice of a very ample sheaf and affine projective charts; coherent finiteness as cited.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-twist-global-generation] to the ample $H$ and the coherent module $L$. For every sufficiently large $n\geq1$, $F_n=L\otimes H^{\otimes(n-1)}$ is globally generated. Fix $x\in A$. Choose a section $s$ of $H$ whose affine nonvanishing chart contains $x$, and a generating section $t$ of $F_n$ nonzero at $x$. Then $s\otimes t$ is a section of $H\otimes F_n=M_n$ and [lem-sc-tensor-section-affine-open] gives $A_{s\otimes t}=A_s\cap A_t$, affine and containing $x$. Thus the affine-locus condition holds for $M_n$ at every point. By [lem-pc-ample-affine-loci-criterion], $M_n$ is ample. This proves eventual ampleness directly; it is not an additional prerequisite node.

source.place: Elementary affine-locus argument of Tag 0890, lemma-ample-tensor-globally-generated, using the cited generation and affine intersection statements.

proof.text: For every sufficiently large $n$, the generating sections of $F_n$ in step 2 and the coordinate sections of $H$ give a tensor section of $M_n$ nonzero at the identity. By [lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization], $A$ is integral. Thus [lem-pc-nonzero-section-integral-cartier] and [lem-pc-zero-scheme-divisor-iso] give an effective Cartier divisor $E_n$ with $M_n\cong\mathcal O_A(E_n)$. Its ampleness from step 2 now implies, by the effective-divisor clause of [lem-sfb-abelian-polarization-calculus], that $f_n=\phi_{M_n}$ is an isogeny. The same reasoning with a nonzero coordinate section of $H$ proves that $\phi_H$ is an isogeny. This uses neither theta-group representations nor the Euler-square identity.

source.place: I Proposition 8.1 and Remark 8.2; effective-divisor criterion applied after producing an actual section.

proof.text:
Put $a:A\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and fix one of these $M=M_n$. By [lem-sc-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free], $V=e_A^*\Omega^1_{A/k}$ has dimension $g$. The identity in [lem-sfb-group-scheme-differentials-from-identity] gives $\Omega^1_{A/k}\cong\mathcal O_A\otimes_kV$. Choose a basis of $V$; its top wedge trivializes $\omega_A=\bigwedge^g\Omega^1_{A/k}$. Now [lem-sc-smooth-proper-relative-dualizing-general] gives $a^!k\cong\mathcal O_A[g]$, where $a^!$ is the right adjoint of $R\Gamma(A,-)$. For every integer $j$ its adjunction gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(M,\mathcal O_A[g+j])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(k)}(R\Gamma(A,M),k[j]).$$
Tensoring by the invertible module $M^{-1}$ identifies the left side with $H^{g+j}(A,M^{-1})$: tensoring by $M$ and $M^{-1}$ are mutually inverse exact functors, hence mutually inverse on complexes and their derived categories. The right side has dimension $\dim_k H^{-j}(A,M)$: a bounded complex of finite-dimensional vector spaces splits, by choosing complements to boundaries in cycles and to cycles in each term, into its cohomology and contractible two-term complexes. Taking the alternating dimension sums and reindexing $i=g+j$ gives
$$\chi(A,M^{-1})=(-1)^g\chi(A,M).$$
This is a direct adjunction calculation with the cited dualizing object, independent of abelian Riemann–Roch.

source.place: Tag 0BRT, lemma-smooth-proper; specialize its right-adjoint identification to the field and use the invariant differential frame.

proof.text:
Keep $M=M_n$, write $f=\phi_M$ and $K=\ker f$, with inclusion $i:K\hookrightarrow A$. On $A\times A$ put
$$\Lambda=m^*M\otimes p_1^*M^{-1}\otimes p_2^*M^{-1}.$$
The normalized-family identity of [lem-sfb-abelian-polarization-calculus] identifies $\Lambda$ with $(1\times f)^*\mathcal P_A$ (a constant one-dimensional factor may be trivialized). By [lem-sc-isogeny-degree], $f$ is finite flat. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-resolution-iso] to $p_2:A\times A^\vee\to A^\vee$ and the flat base change $f$. The derived comparison is an isomorphism because its maps on all cohomology sheaves are precisely the isomorphisms in that statement; flat pullback is exact. Together with [lem-sfb-poincare-coherent-transform] this gives
$$Rp_{2*}\Lambda\simeq f^*(e_*k)[-g]\simeq i_*\mathcal O_K[-g].$$
The last identification is local tensor algebra: if $J$ is the identity ideal on an affine base chart, its pullback is the module $B\otimes_C(C/J)=B/JB$ defining the scheme-theoretic fibre. Thus the whole kernel, including nilpotents, occurs.

source.place: §16 pp.151–152: flat base change of the §13 Poincare calculation; Stacks Tag 02KH is supplied by the existing base-change node.

proof.text:
The line module $M$ is perfect. The projection formula [lem-sbc-ringed-site-perfect-projection-formula] applied to $p_2$ therefore identifies
$$Rp_{2*}(\Lambda\otimes p_2^*M)\simeq(i_*\mathcal O_K\otimes M)[-g]\simeq i_*(i^*M)[-g].$$
The second isomorphism is the finite projection map of [lem-sfb-finite-map-locally-free-euler-comparison], for $i$. The same node gives $\chi(A,i_*N)=\chi(K,N)$ for $N=i^*M$ and $\mathcal O_K$. The finite $k$-scheme $K$ is Noetherian and zero-dimensional: its affine coordinate algebra is finite-dimensional, and its domain quotients are fields. By [lem-sc-zero-dim-noetherian-finite-discrete] its points are open singletons. Restrict a local frame of $N$ to each singleton and glue the frames over this disjoint open cover; thus $N\cong\mathcal O_K$, even when $K$ is nonreduced. By [lem-pc-affine-vanishing], $\chi(K,N)=\dim_k\Gamma(K,\mathcal O_K)=d(f)$. Composition of derived direct images [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image-composition] permits taking $R\Gamma$ of these identities, and the shift contributes $(-1)^g$. Consequently
$$\chi(A\times A,\Lambda)=\chi(A\times A,\Lambda\otimes p_2^*M)=(-1)^g d(f).$$

source.place: §16 pp.151–152: twisting a finite-support direct image does not change its Euler characteristic; projection, finite-map Euler comparison and composition are cited explicitly.

proof.text:
The tensor product $\Lambda\otimes p_2^*M$ is $m^*M\otimes p_1^*M^{-1}$. The map $u:A\times A\to A\times A$, $(x,y)\mapsto(x+y,x)$, is an isomorphism with inverse $(v,w)\mapsto(w,v-w)$. It pulls $p_1^*M\otimes p_2^*M^{-1}$ back to this tensor product. Change of coordinates by this isomorphism preserves coherent cohomology. Apply [lem-sc-picard-kunneth-qcoh] with the coherent modules $M$ and $M^{-1}$: $A$ is quasi-compact and separated, hence has affine diagonal. Taking the finite alternating dimension sums gives
$$\chi(A\times A,\Lambda\otimes p_2^*M)=\sum_{r,s}(-1)^{r+s}\dim H^r(A,M)\dim H^s(A,M^{-1})=\chi(A,M)\chi(A,M^{-1}).$$
Step 4 makes this $(-1)^g\chi(A,M)^2$. Compare with step 6 and cancel $(-1)^g$. We have proved $d(\phi_{M_n})=\chi(A,M_n)^2$ for every sufficiently large $n$.

source.place: §16 pp.151–152: the automorphism (m,p1), coherent Kunneth (Stacks Tag 0BED), and the inverse-bundle Euler sign.

proof.text:
The representing Picard functor in [lem-sfb-abelian-polarization-calculus] has tensor product as addition. For invertible modules $B,C$, the identity
$$t_x^*(B\otimes C)\otimes(B\otimes C)^{-1}\cong(t_x^*B\otimes B^{-1})\otimes(t_x^*C\otimes C^{-1})$$
holds functorially on every test scheme and respects the rigidifications. Thus the represented homomorphisms satisfy $\phi_{B\otimes C}=\phi_B+\phi_C$. Inducting on $n$ gives $\phi_{M_n}=\phi_L+n\phi_H$ for $n\geq0$. This is an identity of group-scheme homomorphisms, obtained from families, not just from their values on $k$-points.

source.place: I §§5 and 8: tensor product in the represented Picard group functor; direct substitution in the translation family.

proof.text: Step 3 gives an isogeny $\phi_H:A\to A^\vee$. The last assertion of [lem-sfb-simple-isogeny-decomposition] supplies an isogeny $q:A^\vee\to A$. Put $a=q\circ\phi_L$ and $b=q\circ\phi_H$ in $\operatorname{End}_k(A)$. In the rational endomorphism space, take the subspace spanned by $a\otimes1,b\otimes1$, of dimension at most two. On any basis of that subspace, [lem-sfb-abelian-degree-polynomial] represents degree by a rational polynomial. Substitute the coordinates of $(a+nb)\otimes1$ into this polynomial. Each coordinate is affine linear in $n$, so the substitution gives $Q\in\mathbf Q[T]$ with $Q(n)=d(a+nb)$ for every integer $n$. No independence of $a,b$ is assumed.

source.place: I, Remark 8.6 (quasi-inverse isogeny), Remark 10.11 and Proposition 10.13 (degree polynomial); affine-linear substitution written out.

proof.text:
The varieties $A,A^\vee,A$ have the same positive dimension by [lem-sfb-abelian-polarization-calculus]. Apply [lem-sfb-isogeny-postcomposition-degree] to $h=\phi_{M_n}$ and $u=q$. It gives
$$Q(n)=d(q\phi_{M_n})=(\deg q)d(\phi_{M_n})\qquad(n\geq0),$$
including those $n$ for which $\phi_{M_n}$ is not an isogeny. Since $q$ is an isogeny, $c=\deg q$ is positive: its finite kernel contains its identity section, so its coordinate algebra has positive dimension. Set $D(T)=c^{-1}Q(T)$. Then $D(n)=d(\phi_{M_n})$ for every $n\geq0$, in particular $D(0)=d(\phi_L)$.

source.place: I §7 and Remark 8.6, including the zero convention before Theorem 10.9; use the cited postcomposition lemma also in the non-isogeny case.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-snapper-numerical-polynomial] to the proper $k$-scheme $A$, the coherent module $L$, and the single invertible sheaf $H$. It gives a numerical polynomial $P\in\mathbf Q[T]$ with $P(n)=\chi(A,L\otimes H^{\otimes n})$ for all integers $n$, so in particular $P(0)=\chi(A,L)$.

source.place: Tag 0BEL, lemma-numerical-polynomial-from-euler, with one twisting sheaf.

proof.text: By step 7, $D(n)-P(n)^2=0$ for every sufficiently large integer $n$. These give infinitely many distinct rational roots. A nonzero polynomial over $\mathbf Q$ has at most its degree many roots (successively divide by $T-n$), so $D=P^2$. Evaluating at $0$ yields $d(\phi_L)=D(0)=P(0)^2=\chi(A,L)^2$. The equality holds in $\mathbf Q$ and hence in $\mathbf Z$ since both sides are integers. This also covers $d(\phi_L)=0$, without assuming $L$ is ample or $\phi_L$ an isogeny.
